proof_sketch_tex: Linear pushforward of the standard Gaussian gives the real Gaussian variance $\|y\|^2$. Its even moments follow from derivatives of the MGF. Polarization of the fourth power gives the mixed squared-projection formula; a second polarization gives the full fourth-product Wick identity. Expand a bilinear quadratic form in any orthonormal basis, integrate its squared expansion, and use Wick and Parseval to obtain the trace-square plus twice the sum of coefficient squares. Cauchy--Schwarz then yields the existing dimension-dependent lower bound.
